# CLAUDE.md

This file provides guidance to Claude Code (claude.ai/code) when working with code in this repository.

## What this is

A slim, **Drive-only** subset of `google/apiclient-services` (~670 KB of `Google\Service\Drive`
classes instead of the 200+ service, 200MB+ monorepo). The package is an unofficial,
community-maintained derivative — **not affiliated with Google** (see `NOTICE`). Apache-2.0,
matching upstream.

**The single most important rule:** everything under `src/` is **generated by Google and synced
from upstream** (`googleapis/google-api-php-client-services`). Do **not** hand-edit those files —
the next sync overwrites them. Per-file `Copyright 2014 Google Inc.` headers must never be
stripped (Apache-2.0 attribution requirement). Work that changes `src/` belongs in the sync
tooling, not in manual edits. Non-generated repo files (`tools/`, `tests/`, `composer.json`,
`README.md`, `CLAUDE.md`, etc.) are fair game.

## Commands

```bash
composer validate --strict --no-check-publish        # validate manifest
composer install                                 # installs dev deps (phpunit, roave) — see testing note
php -l src/Drive.php                             # lint a single file
find src -name '*.php' -exec php -l {} +         # lint all generated source

vendor/bin/phpunit                               # all tests + coverage (phpunit.xml.dist is configured)
vendor/bin/phpunit --filter testNoCrossServiceNamespaceReferences   # one test
php tools/coverage-check.php build/clover.xml 95 # enforce the 95% min coverage gate from the Clover report

vendor/bin/roave-backward-compatibility-check --from=<ref> --to=<ref>   # BC check (see caveat)
```

`phpunit.xml.dist` configures the `src/` coverage target (PCOV) and emits `build/clover.xml`. The
suite is 110 tests / 100% line coverage. PHPUnit 10 has no native min-coverage threshold, so
`tools/coverage-check.php` parses the Clover report and exits non-zero below the threshold (this
is what CI gates on).

## Architecture

**Namespace layout** mirrors upstream's PSR-4 map exactly (`Google\Service\` → `src`), making
this a drop-in for `google/apiclient-services` namespace-wise:

- `src/Drive.php` — `Google\Service\Drive`, the service entry point. Extends `Google\Service`,
  declares the OAuth scope constants (`DRIVE`, `DRIVE_READONLY`, …), and wires up 14 resource
  collections (`$this->files`, `$this->about`, `$this->permissions`, …) in its constructor.
- `src/Drive/*.php` — 76 generated **model** classes (`DriveFile`, `About`, `Change`, …)
  extending `Google\Model` or `Google\Collection`; each declares `public $prop` plus a
  `set*/get*` pair (verified to be pure `$this->prop = $val; return $this;` assignments).
- `src/Drive/Resource/*.php` — 16 **resource** classes (`Files`, `Permissions`, `About`, …)
  extending `Google\Service\Resource`; each method is a thin
  `return $this->call('name', [$params], ExpectedClass::class)`.

**The base classes are not in this repo and not in `apiclient-services`.** `Google\Client`,
`Google\Service`, `Google\Model`, `Google\Collection`, `Google\Service\Resource`, and
`Google\Service\Exception` live in the **`google/apiclient`** core package. This package only
ships the Drive-specific generated classes — which is *why* a file-level extraction is safe:

**The cross-service isolation invariant.** Drive's generated classes reference no other
`Google\Service\*` namespace — only `Google\Service\Drive`, plus the shared
`Google\Service\Resource` / `Google\Service\Exception` base classes.
`AutoloadSmokeTest::testNoCrossServiceNamespaceReferences` enforces this in tests, and the sync
script's guard grep enforces it on fetched files. The grep is **anchored** (`Google\Service\Drive$`)
so a real sibling service like `Google\Service\DriveActivity` is not filtered out as a substring
of `Google\Service\Drive`. Do not weaken these guards.

The full design is in `apiclient-drive-service-plan.md` — **read it before changing `tools/` or
the workflow.** That file is intentionally kept untracked: never `git add` it, never gitignore it.

## Testing & the google/apiclient conflict

`google/apiclient` is **not** a hard `require` — it is a `suggest`. Reason: `google/apiclient`
itself hard-requires `google/apiclient-services`, which this package `conflict`s with. So
`composer install` gets you phpunit + roave, **but not** `google/apiclient` — `Google\Client`,
`Google\Model`, `Google\Service\Resource`, etc. are undefined at test time.

`tests/Stubs/google_apiclient_stubs.php` provides minimal-but-faithful structural stubs for those
base classes. `tests/bootstrap.php` loads them whenever `!class_exists(\Google\Client::class)`
(regardless of whether `vendor/autoload.php` exists — the original early-return on
`file_exists(vendor/autoload.php)` was a bug that left 16/18 tests failing). The stubs:
- `Resource` has a no-op `call()` so generated resource method bodies execute for coverage.
- `Service` declares upstream's public props + `getClient()` (avoids dynamic-property deprecations).
- `Model` has `#[\AllowDynamicProperties]` (matches upstream).

Coverage is **100% via reflection** (`tests/Generated/`): `ModelStructuralTest` instantiates every
model and round-trips each setter/getter; `ResourceStructuralTest` invokes every own public method
on each resource. This is structural integrity (instantiable, setters accept type-appropriate
values, getters return exactly what was stored), not business behavior — the only sane way to
cover ~18k LOC of generated code. Don't add hand-written per-class getter/setter tests (low value);
the BC check + smoke test + reflection suite are the intended safety net.

## Sync pipeline & versioning

Implemented (not just planned): `tools/sync-from-upstream.sh` + `.github/workflows/sync.yml` +
`.github/workflows/stale-check.yml`.

The weekly sync uses a **blobless partial clone + non-cone `git sparse-checkout`** to pull only
`src/Drive.php` + `src/Drive/*` + `LICENSE` from upstream (~670 KB). `--no-cone` is mandatory —
cone mode grabs all 200+ sibling top-level service files (16 MB). Three guards run before
staging: cross-service-reference grep (anchored), filename length ≤ 139 chars (the PSR-4
autoload-shim threshold), and non-empty extraction.

**Dry-run by design:** the workflow runs the tests + 95% coverage gate on the synced code, then
**opens a PR** — it never auto-tags or publishes. A daily `stale-check.yml` fails if the sync
workflow hasn't *succeeded* in 7 days (a no-change week still exits 0, so it doesn't false-alarm).

**BC checking is NOT automated.** Roave/BackwardCompatibilityCheck could not resolve the
`google/apiclient` base classes (suggest-only + conflict), emitting only spurious
`ReflectionClass "Google\Model" could not be found` breaks. Review the sync PR diff manually.

Versioning is SemVer, decided manually on merge: PATCH (cosmetic), MINOR (additive), MAJOR
(breaking). The package starts at `1.0.0` (not yet tagged).

## Distribution constraints

- `conflict` with `google/apiclient-services` (not `provide`/`replace`) — masquerading as the full
  catalog would let Composer resolve cleanly and then fatal-error at runtime. **Known caveat:**
  conflict-without-`provide` currently makes the package uninstallable alongside `google/apiclient`
  (which hard-requires `apiclient-services`) — adding `provide: { google/apiclient-services: "*" }`
  is the verified fix and is under consideration.
- `.gitattributes` `export-ignore`s `/.github`, `/tools`, `/tests`, `/CLAUDE.md`, etc. so the
  Composer dist archive ships runtime code + legal docs only. `composer.lock` is intentionally not
  committed (this is a library, not an application).
